question: Electrons are accelerated through a potential difference of $54\,\text{V}$. Calculate their de Broglie wavelength using $\lambda = \frac{12.27}{\sqrt{V}}\,\text{Å}$. How is this result related to the Davisson and Germer experiment?

options.A: $\lambda=\dfrac{12.27}{54}\,\text{Å}\approx0.23\,\text{Å}$; this proves electrons have no wave nature.
options.B: $\lambda=\dfrac{12.27}{\sqrt{54}}\,\text{Å}\approx12.27\,\text{Å}$; it is unrelated to the experiment.
options.C: $\lambda=\dfrac{12.27}{\sqrt{54}}\,\text{Å}\approx3.34\,\text{Å}$; it shows that electron wavelength is much larger than atomic spacing.
options.D: $\lambda=\dfrac{12.27}{\sqrt{54}}\,\text{Å}\approx1.67\,\text{Å}$. Its agreement with the wavelength obtained from electron diffraction in the Davisson and Germer experiment confirmed the wave nature of electrons.
